newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges quick probe of Syria bombing.
newsitem.headline: France urges quick probe of Syria bombing.

text.p: France said on Friday that the bombing of a bus in Damascus showed that all nations faced a terrorist threat and hoped those responsible for the blast could be quickly identified.

"The French government condemns all acts of violence, whatever their origin and whoever is responsible for them. It hopes that light will quickly be shed on this attack," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Syria has accused Israeli agents of planting the bomb on the bus as part of attempts to derail the Middle East peace process. Syrian authorities said the blast killed nine people and wounded 44.
Israel denied being behind the New Year's Eve attack and the United States warned Syria against making "wild and irresponsible" statements without evidence.

Rummelhardt did not take sides, saying the bombing "reminds us that that all nations of the world are exposed to the threat of terrorism. This act confirms that everyone must work together to battle senseless violence and search for peace".
French President Jacques Chirac has actively courted Arab states, including Syria, in recent months in an effort to carve out a bigger role for Paris in the Middle East peace process.
